records.text: Ronald Reagan Washington National, Dulles, Baltimore/Washington, and Richmond airports were all shut down for about two hours and twenty minutes, initially attributed to a strong odor from the Potomac River and later to an overheated circuit board.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: DCA, both Ronald Reagan Airport and Dulles Airport, which is in D.C., plus Baltimore Airport, which is the nearest, plus Richmond Airport, which would be also just outside of D.C., all of them just got shut down. ... And they said because there was a strong odor coming from the Potomac River. ... What? It was shut down for about two hours, 20 minutes. And then when they came back, they said that the there was a circuit board that overheated.

verification.notes: FAA and AP reporting confirms ground stops at Reagan National, Dulles, BWI, and Richmond due to a strong chemical smell at Potomac TRACON, later traced by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy to an overheated circuit board. The ground stop lasted over an hour; roughly two-hour delays followed. The transcript's two-hours-twenty duration conflates the halt with delays.

sources.title: A strong chemical smell forces a 1-hour flight halt at 4 major DC-area airports
sources.relevance: Confirms the four airports, cause, and duration over an hour.

sources.title: Ground stop at DC-area airports lifted after strong chemical smell
sources.relevance: Confirms Duffy's overheated-circuit-board explanation and ensuing delays.

records.text: The overheated-circuit-board explanation for shutting down four Washington-area airports was a lie; it seemed officials were trying to move someone in or out while keeping other aircraft away.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: They didn't say where that circuit board overheated, but that was the reason they shut down four airports around the White House. ... No, that's obviously a lie. Something happened to me. It's like they were trying to get somebody in or get somebody out. They didn't want anybody else in the air. ... That's my opinion. Obviously not a fact.

verification.notes: Owens explicitly labeled the proposed movement of an unidentified person as her opinion. Authoritative reporting says a chemical odor at Potomac TRACON was traced to an overheated circuit board and records no evidence that the shutdown was staged to move someone. Absence of evidence does not meet the strict false standard for this speculative allegation.

sources.title: A strong chemical smell forces a 1-hour flight halt at 4 major DC-area airports
sources.relevance: Provides the official operational explanation and no support for the movement theory.
